target.name: NetworkOcean
target.founder: Sam Mendel (CEO; serial founder, prior exit of a creator-hiring marketplace), Eric Kim (CTO; ex-Palantir, Merge; Cornell)

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $1M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
NetworkOcean is a seed-stage ocean and maritime company founded by Sam Mendel, a serial founder with a prior marketplace exit, and Eric Kim, formerly of Palantir and Merge. The company has raised $1M to date. The comp universe consists of three private peers in the ocean and maritime sector—Standard Subsea, Clippership, and Albacore—with no relevant public comparables identified.

The stage-progression method applies a 2.5x multiplier to the $1M raised as a proxy for current valuation, reflecting typical Seed-to-next-stage step-ups in the frontier-tech maritime space. This method yields an implied valuation of $2.5M. The analytical range narrows to $2.125M–$2.875M, with a median of $2.5M supported by this single triangulation method.

Key uncertainties warrant explicit flagging: the analysis relies on only one valuation method due to data constraints, and no public comparables exist to benchmark against. The private peer set is small and available metrics for those companies are not provided, limiting relative-value calibration. The founder team's quality—particularly Mendel's prior exit and Kim's data-infrastructure background—is qualitatively favorable but not quantified into the analysis. A post-seed valuation should incorporate detailed revenue projections, customer traction, and explicit positioning against the three private peers before finalizing terms.
